_doc: Pre-registered review windows, kill rules, and triggers for the bot fleet.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: two pre-registrations rotted silently in May 2026 —
the FF ARB 3rd-loss trigger (fired 2026-05-14, evaluated 26 days late) and
the CascadeFader 30-day dry-run gate (expired 2026-06-08 unevaluated) —
because they lived only in commit messages and session memory.
Every entry with status 'open' is surfaced in the daily health report
(strategy_health_report.py, PRE-REGISTRATIONS section) with an OVERDUE
marker once review_by passes. Closing an entry requires a human decision
recorded in 'resolution'. New pre-registrations MUST be added here, not
(only) in commit messages or memory.
'rules' is free text for humans. 'triggers' is the machine-checkable subset
the daily report actually evaluates: {id, metric, basis, op, threshold,
action}. Only metric 'max_drawdown_pct' is auto-evaluated today; basis is
'full_run', 'since_registered', or 'both' (breaches on the worse reading —
the conservative default when the rule's wording does not pin a denominator).
Anything expressible as a trigger SHOULD be one: on 2026-07-29 a drawdown
trigger fired and went unseen for two days because it lived only in 'rules'.
Never edit a rule in place. Changing what a pre-registration commits to
requires an entry in 'amendments' recording the reason — that is the whole
point of pre-registering. Disagreeing with a past rule is legitimate;
disagreeing with it silently is not.

rules: Rollback gate v2 if account MaxDD > 3.60% (1.5x backtest 2.40%)

If <10 closed trades by review_by, the PF rule is NOT evaluable: review must instead compare gate-open time vs backtest expectation and decide extend/simplify, not auto-pass

amendments.conflict_found: Two texts disagree on BOTH threshold and action. Commit 34ec07b (2026-05-19, the actual pre-declaration): 'Demote to regime-halt-only if live MaxDD > 3.84% (1.5x backtest). Kill if DD > 8% or 5+ consecutive losses or PF < 0.7 over 30+ trades.' This registry entry (added 2026-06-09): 'Rollback gate v2 if account MaxDD > 3.60%.' The registry silently changed the number AND the action, in opposite directions — 'demote to regime-halt-only' keeps the restrictive filter (bot trades less), 'rollback gate v2' removes it (bot trades more). 3.84% is also arithmetically odd: the commit says '1.5x backtest' but 1.5 x 2.40 = 3.60, so 3.84 (=1.6x) looks like the original slip and 3.60 like a correction that overreached into the action clause. RESOLUTION: both texts are recorded as separate triggers above; neither is discarded. All three thresholds are breached.
amendments.measurement: Closed-equity MaxDD, freqtrade /profit basis. Full-run 8.60% (peak $86.46 on 2026-05-10 -> trough $79.03 on 2026-07-29; abs $7.43). Gate-v2-era only (peak re-baselined at 2026-05-19 equity $82.60) 4.32%, same trough date. Starting capital $80.65; bot-owned equity $78.91 at audit. NOTE: the '$200 live' figure in older session notes is wrong — the API reports ~$80.
amendments.decision: THREE pre-committed actions are in scope and NONE was executed. (a) 'Rollback gate v2' at 3.60% (registry) — breached, not executed. (b) 'Demote to regime-halt-only' at 3.84% (34ec07b) — breached, not executed. (c) 'KILL if DD > 8%' (34ec07b) — breached on the full-run reading (8.60%), NOT breached on the gate-v2-era reading (4.32%); not executed. Instead FundingFadeV1 was PAUSED: no new entries, open positions still fully managed (exits, ROI, stoploss and timeouts all run in PAUSED state — verified in freqtrade 2026.3 source, exit_positions() is unconditional in FreqtradeBot.process() and only entry is gated on state == RUNNING). The pause was also made durable in FundingFadeV1.live.json (initial_state running -> paused), because PAUSED is in-memory only and any restart, redeploy or VPS reboot would otherwise have silently resumed live trading.
amendments.kill_arm_override: STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT WOULD BE EASY TO BURY: pausing is a WEAKER action than the kill this pre-registration commits to. The kill arm fired and was overridden, not satisfied. It is an open override requiring operator sign-off, and it is live NOW — it is not deferred to 2026-08-17 and must not be treated as resolved by the pause. Two things make the override defensible rather than an evasion, and neither makes it automatic: (1) the kill arm's denominator is genuinely ambiguous in the same way the demote arm's is — it fires at 8.60% full-run but not at 4.32% gate-v2-era, and the full-run figure includes a drawdown whose peak (2026-05-10) predates the pre-registration by nine days, so the clause is being read against a window it was not written for; (2) with the bot paused and the position book down to one trade running to its own stoploss, the practical gap between pause and kill is capital allocation, not risk taken. If the operator wants the pre-commitment honoured literally, the action is to kill: stop the container and withdraw the allocation. That decision is his, and declining to make it is itself a decision that should be recorded here. The other two kill sub-clauses did NOT fire: max consecutive losses within the gate-v2 era is 3, not 5 (the full-run streak of 7 spans the May window that predates the declaration), and the PF arm needs 30+ closed trades against 6 actual.
amendments.rationale: This covers the two gate arms only; the kill arm is dealt with separately in kill_arm_override. Both gate actions LOOSEN the gate. That made sense when written: the rule is a falsification clause — gate v2 promised MaxDD 2.40%, so exceeding 1.5x means the filter did not deliver and you stop paying its cost in trade scarcity. But it was written 2026-05-19, BEFORE the OOS retest of 2026-07-13 established that the problem is not gate tightness: the gate was open 23.4% of the OOS window (backtest era 33.3%) and those 310 gate-open hours produced ONE funding signal against a claimed 1.67/wk. The signal decayed, not the gate. Executing either action today would put real money on a LOOSER version of a strategy with live gate-v2-era PF 0.078 (1W/5L, every loss a full -5% stop) and no demonstrated OOS edge. Corroboration that this is structural and not a small-N artifact: hl-carry-shadow-2026-07 has recorded ZERO episodes in 18 days because max trailing-24h funding across 40 coins is 10.95%/yr against a 40%/yr entry — the same funding-yield compression, on a different venue, measured by a different instrument.
amendments.statistical_honesty: N=6 closed trades since registration cannot establish that the edge is dead; the confidence interval is very wide, and the 2026-07-12 ADA loss was a known funding-freshness fault since fixed. The honest characterization is 'severe adverse live evidence and payoff realization inconsistent with the backtest, too few independent trades for a reliable edge estimate'. The pause is justified by the drawdown trigger and the OOS signal-scarcity finding, NOT by a claim that N=6 proves anything.
amendments.open_for_operator: TWO open items, different clocks. (1) OPEN NOW, not deferrable: sign off on or reject the kill-arm override described in kill_arm_override. The pause does not settle it — 'the bot is paused so nothing fires' is true of the two gate-loosening actions and FALSE of the kill. (2) Deferrable to 2026-08-17: which text is authoritative for the demote/rollback arms (34ec07b vs registry). That one genuinely can wait, because both candidate actions loosen a gate on a paused bot and neither can fire while it stays paused.
amendments.provenance: The pause was first applied at 2026-07-31 03:29:46 UTC by an unintended state-changing API call during this audit (a POST issued while probing endpoint availability), not by a deliberate decision. It was reported to the operator immediately with a revert command offered; the operator reviewed the finding and confirmed the pause as the intended action in the same session. Recorded because a governance file must not launder how its own state came about.

Loosening the filter as a response to a drawdown would move to a configuration that tested worse on the very metric that triggered.
amendments.why_not_demote_to_regime_halt: Also moot. Both contested texts argue about WHICH filter to run, while the record says the signal stopped working WITH gate v2 active: first 12 closed trades PF 4.77 (+$5.81), last 12 PF 0.08 (-$7.13, 11 losses in 12). The filter built to prevent exactly that regime did not prevent it. Changing filter configuration does not address that.
amendments.why_the_pre_v2_record_counts: The 2026-08-23 V2 epoch changed EXECUTION (custom_exit activation, exchange-resident stops), not the entry signal or the macro gate. The trades that produced PF 0.08 would be selected identically under V2, so the pre-V2 record is informative about V2's signal quality. V2 itself has 1 trade in 7 days — no evidence either way.
amendments.reversal_condition: Re-fund only on a preregistered change to the SIGNAL or the gate, justified out of sample, not on a favourable dry stretch. The strategy is regime-dependent by design (docstring: 2024 PF 1.80, 2026 PF 0.74); a good month is expected noise, not evidence.

amendments.reason: The 2026-08-30 demotion is REVERSED. It was based on a miscount.
amendments.error: The claim was '7 consecutive losses against a kill clause of 5+'. The losses were counted consecutive in a result-ordered list WITHOUT checking dates. By date they are two separate blocks with a 52-day no-trade gap between them: 2026-05-11/13/15/15/16 (five), then nothing until 2026-07-11/12 (two). Not one streak, and the clause was never met by the second block.
amendments.double_jeopardy: The May 10-16 block IS the 5-SL streak that already triggered its own remediation — gate v2, deployed 2026-05-19. The operator's response at the time was to fix, not to kill. Re-applying a kill clause to the same streak three months later judges the same event twice.
amendments.known_cause_already_fixed: The two July losses (HBAR 07-11, ADA 07-12) were diagnosed as the stale-funding defect — ADA traded on funding data 10h old — and fixed 2026-07-13 (commit 177cdd1, hourly :10 refresh). Counting them as evidence against the strategy counts a data bug as a signal failure.
amendments.why_the_pf_figure_was_also_wrong: The quoted 'last 12 trades PF 0.08' spans BOTH sides of the 2026-05-19 gate-v2 deploy and both sides of the 2026-07-13 funding fix, so it aggregates three different versions of the strategy. Post-gate-v2 AND post-funding-fix there are only four closed trades (SUI 07-24, ZEC 07-27, LTC 07-29, NEAR 07-31). That is not a sample; it is not evidence of failure either.
amendments.what_is_actually_true: There is essentially NO post-remediation sample for this strategy. The honest position is neither 'it failed' nor 'it works' — it is unmeasured. The V2 epoch DB (from 2026-08-23) is the correct measurement object and holds one open trade.
amendments.corrected_trigger_scope: Drawdown and consecutive-loss triggers must be evaluated on the CURRENT epoch DB only (tradesv3.live.FundingFadeV1.v2.sqlite), never on the frozen pre-V2 curve, and consecutive-loss counting must be date-ordered with a maximum gap, not merely adjacent rows in a result list.

Per-pair funding now fails closed at _STALE_FUNDING_HOURS (12h) in _align_to_dataframe, matching the macro gate; previously it only warned while forward-filling frozen funding into live bars indefinitely. The 'shadow-log first' stage was COLLAPSED: it existed to avoid changing entry behaviour mid-measurement on a running bot, and FF is paused (see ff-gate-v2-review amendment), so there is no live measurement to disturb. preregistrations.method: Per dry fill (entries, TP-ladder partials): fetch Binance futures 1m klines for the window; STRICT scenario = limit fill counts at posted price only if 1m price strictly trades through (long entry L: low < L; short/TP sells: high > TP); TOUCH scenario = touch counts (current dry behavior, upper bound). SL/market exits re-priced taker with 0.05% adverse slippage. Recompute P&L/WR/DD per scenario over the full dry period.

STRICT re-priced P&L <= 0 -> dry-run fill optimism confirmed forward; do-not-fund RECONFIRMED; no tuning study
0 < STRICT P&L < +10% -> inconclusive; continue measuring, no tuning, revisit at next review

why_this_direction_and_not_the_other: The research note offers two coherent designs — a counter-trend fade gated on volatility/funding extremes, or a trend-continuation short triggered on breakdowns. Continuation is the better fit HERE for a venue-specific reason: Hyperliquid pays roughly 10.4% APR to hold a short. A design that holds through a downtrend is PAID to wait; a fast fade collects almost none of that carry. The same funding carry is what made the current design's ceiling uneconomic.
The current design was closed for every hour of the 2025-10-10 cascade — it structurally misses the events a short strategy exists to capture. A breakdown trigger fires DURING cascades.
It is the minimal change: the gate, the volume filter and the channel geometry are all reused, so exactly one term moves and the redesign stays attributable.

measured_frequency.method: Reconstructed both triggers against the SAME macro gate over 14,400 hourly bars (2025-01-07..2026-08-30) on BTC/ETH/SOL. Frequency only — deliberately no P&L, no exit modelling, no threshold sweep.
measured_frequency.validation: The reconstruction reproduces the 2026-08-29 research note's headline exactly (4 signals, 0.20/month), which is what licenses trusting the comparison.
measured_frequency.result: A (deployed, rejection): 4 signals, 0.20/month, N=30 in 12.3 years. B (proposed, breakdown): 158 signals, 8.01/month, N=30 in ~4 months. Without the volume filter B would be 272 / 13.78 per month, so volume is doing real work and stays.

Binance USDT klines are a proxy for Hyperliquid USDC candles. Volume distributions are NOT comparable and volume is a binding filter, so HL counts will differ.
8 signals/month across 3 pairs may prove too many once costs are applied. That is a validatable rate, which is the entire point — 0.20/month is not.

phase1: Window: announcements dated 2023-01-01 00:00 UTC to 2026-10-31 23:59 UTC. The start is roughly when Hyperliquid perps begin to exist. Nothing after the window enters this study.
Events, delisting study (Claude's call):
Counted: one event per (announcement, token) for two kinds of notice:
a full Binance spot delisting, where the token loses every spot pair;
a new monitoring-tag assignment.
Excluded:
removal of individual trading pairs where the token keeps at least one spot pair;
margin-only and futures-only delistings;
vote-to-delist and similar polls;
removals of a tag.
Retractions and corrections stay in. They are unknowable at entry time.
Classification: from the notice text as harvested. The CMS returns current versions, so later edits cannot be ruled out; this is recorded as a limitation.
Overlap: if the same token has a second qualifying notice within 24 h of the first, only the first counts. Notices more than 24 h apart are separate events.
One test: both kinds share one pass/fail. Per-kind results are reported as descriptive only.
Timestamps:
Binance: `releaseDate`.
Upbit: the builder documents whether `listed_at` or `first_listed_at` is the publish time. The prereg names the field before Phase 1 runs.
Execution venues (Claude's call): Binance futures is CVM-blocked for the operator (see the `listing-reaction-study-2026-07` notes), so only these count:
Delisting study (short): Hyperliquid perp only. Binance spot cannot short.

Hyperliquid eligibility needs positive pre-entry evidence (changed after both rounds; evidence source changed by §11 call 14). A token qualifies only if Hyperliquid hourly funding records (`fundingHistory`, by coin name) exist for it in the 24 h before t0, including at least one in the last hour before t0. Candles cannot serve: `candleSnapshot` returns only the most recent ~5,000 candles, which at 1 h reach back to about 2026-04 (probe on #229). Nothing after t0 is used for eligibility; using it would exclude exactly the tokens that become untradeable right after the event. Tokens no longer in today's `meta` are looked up by name through `fundingHistory`. The builder confirms in Phase 1 that this works for delisted coins and documents it.
Eligibility that cannot be verified is `unknown`. Unknown events are excluded and counted. An earliest daily candle alone is not enough.
Completeness evidence (changed after round 2).

Pagination (changed after round 3): each Binance catalog (48 and 161, plus monitoring if separate) and the Upbit list are harvested in full, every page. The harvested count must equal the API's reported `total`.
Any shortfall is added to the `missing` count, conservatively assumed to fall inside the window.
If no total is reported, the study is INCONCLUSIVE-by-data.
This also covers the catalog-48 overlap exclusion.

Observed 2026-11-03: Upbit's Cloudflare answered error 1015 to page requests 1.5 s apart, so the full Upbit harvest runs at least 8 s per page. Binance catalog 161 reported `total` 446, and its oldest article is dated 2022-02-17.

Candles (changed after round 3): the exact 1m candles each calculation uses must exist. These are t0−10 min and t0−2 min for the leak test, the entry candle, and each horizon's exit candle. No interpolation and no forward-fill. If any is missing, and the halt rule does not resolve it, the event is `missing`.
Halts after entry (changed after rounds 3–4): if an exit candle is missing because trading halted, the exit is the first candle after trading resumes, within 72 h of that scheduled exit time.
Costs are always subtracted from the net return, whatever the side, never applied to a price.
If trading does not resume within that window, the event is `unresolved`.
`halted` events stay in every criterion.

Any unresolved event makes the study INCONCLUSIVE (changed after rounds 4–5). Their outcomes are outcome-dependent: terminal delistings would vanish. So with one or more `unresolved` events the result is INCONCLUSIVE. There is no imputation shortcut: imputed values can move the median and concentration criteria in either direction.
Coverage gate: `unknown`, `missing` and `unresolved` together above 20% of candidate events make the study INCONCLUSIVE-by-data. So does harvesting that cannot complete within the shared limiter.
Resource budget for Part C (changed after round 3):

detection: Primary: the PIT news archive, read-only. Every 15 s, read with durable cursors over both items (item_pk) and item_revisions (rev_pk); a revised title can turn into a listing.
Take Tree items whose url is an upbit.com/service_center/notice page, and deduplicate them per notice id.
Classify with nes_classify.upbit_addition and upbit_krw_membership (title, plus the body when present), by import.
Upbit notices that mention 거래지원 or 마켓 but don't classify go to an unclassified queue in the status output and are never traded.
Audit: poll api.upbit.com/v1/market/all every 5 min and store each timestamped snapshot. A new KRW-* market with no matched notice is logged as a missed detection.
t0 is Tree's published_at, and received_at is kept too. This is a Tree-clock cohort, and every report says so.
Timing is flagged unverified when published_at is missing, is later than received_at, or lags it by more than 5 min. Unverified events are reported but left out of the comparable cohort.
eligibility: Excluded when the token already trades on Upbit KRW: it is in the last market/all snapshot taken before t0 (no snapshot within 15 min before t0 -> unknown).

Excluded when a Binance new-listing notice for it falls within the 24 h before t0 (the archive's binance_listing source). A notice published after t0 never excludes. Only what the archive had received by t0 counts, revisions included; a notice or revision received later is recorded as descriptive (late) and never excludes.
Excluded when the notice body says trading began before the notice.
Hyperliquid eligibility is the Part C rule (nes_venues.hl_facts / hl_status): the perp is in meta and fundingHistory shows records in the 24 h before t0, including one in the last hour.
comparable_cohort: No known trading start is required (Claude's call, 2026-11-05, implementation). Part C required one, but Tree carries no Upbit notice body and the VPS gets 403 from Upbit's announcements API, so the forward cohort is defined by what a deployable bot can know. This is one more stated difference from Part C, beside the Tree clock, book fills and funding.

When a body is present, the start is read with nes_classify.upbit_trading_start_ms. A start before t0 still excludes the event (began_before_notice); a start at or after t0 gives start_unknown = false. With no body, or no start in it, the event stays comparable with start_unknown = true.

A later observation of the same notice (a duplicate Tree item or a revision) that states a start never creates a second event; it is a versioned evidence record. Received before the entry decision, it counts: a start before t0 excludes the event (began_before_notice) and stops the entry, and one at or after t0 sets start_unknown = false. Received after the entry decision, it is descriptive only.
Descriptive only: krw_market_first_seen_ms, the time of the first market/all snapshot after t0 that lists KRW-<TOKEN>. It never selects events.

status and every resolution report show the start_unknown and krw_market_first_seen counts. The decision metric is over the whole comparable cohort; the subset with start_unknown = false is reported as descriptive only.

A Binance market before t0: Binance 1 m klines (USDⓈ-M fapi/v1/klines first, else spot api/v3/klines, the Part C proxy order) show trading in [t0 - 10 min, t0), counting only candles closed by t0 (open + 60 s <= t0).
The Binance leak test passed: |drift| <= 2% between those klines' closes at t0 - 10 min and t0 - 2 min. The same test on Hyperliquid candles is descriptive.
A timely entry: filled within 2 min of t0 + 5 min. Later entries, up to the 10 min deadline, are delayed and descriptive.
Every other Hyperliquid-eligible event is still measured and reported as the descriptive cohort.
paper_trade: Entry at max(t0 + 5 min, detection): read l2Book and sell about 100 USDC into the bids, then freeze the exchange-valid quantity q (rounded to szDecimals). Record the VWAP, mid, best bid and ask, levels used, book time and any delay.
A book older than 5 s, or depth below q, is rejected for that attempt. Part C priced the close of the 1 m candle that contains t0 + 5 min; the difference is noted, not corrected.
Exit at entry + 24 h: buy back q from the asks, with the same checks. Checkpoints at +30 m and +4 h are book-walk marks of q only.
Fee: 4.5 bps taker on each leg's actual notional. No extra slippage term; the book walk is the slippage.

Funding: rates from finalized fundingHistory records for each hourly settlement during the hold; cashflow q x oraclePx x rate, positive funding pays a short; labelled estimated because oraclePx is observed through metaAndAssetCtxs within +-60 s of each boundary.

A boundary with no rate or no observation inside that tolerance makes the event's funding missing. The net is then incomplete: it stays out of the decision mean and counts as missing in the tipping point.

Excursion: MAE/MFE from 1 m candleSnapshot highs and lows, descriptive price excursion only. It is ok only when every minute of the hold has a candle; otherwise it is retried, then stored as partial with candle counts and labelled partial extrema.
Every scheduled action has a 10 min deadline, including after a restart. Missing the deadline makes the outcome missing; a later recovery is stored as late, never as the scheduled outcome.
Ledger: an append-only JSONL ledger with event ids, idempotent on replay. The resolution reports how many outcomes are missing and gives the A4 tipping point.
resolution: Metric: the announcement-level mean net return of the comparable cohort, computed from book fills, fees and funding.
Interval: the A4 calendar-month block bootstrap, passed level=0.95 explicitly (the helper defaults to 98.33%).
One decision, at 40 events or on 2027-11-05, whichever comes first. The 20- and 30-event reports are descriptive only.
EDGE when the lower bound is above 0, NO EDGE when the upper bound is at or below 0, otherwise NOT DETERMINABLE. No interval (fewer than two months) -> NOT DETERMINABLE.
EDGE authorizes only a proposal for a small live pilot under the graduation gates. NO EDGE closes the lane.
Descriptive: +4 h marks, latency, missed and unclassified notices, MAE, and the non-comparable cohort; also the start_unknown = false subset and krw_market_first_seen_ms.

operationalization: U1 Comparable requirements are each True, False or not established. Any False -> descriptive. Not established (Hyperliquid facts unknown, no market/all snapshot within 15 min, Binance klines unreadable for 24 h, a leak test that could not run, an entry never filled) -> the event stays in the comparable cohort with a missing outcome, so it counts in the tipping point rather than vanishing.

U2 The entry window is [max(t0 + 5 min, detection), t0 + 15 min] on the monitor's clock (book receipt time); timely when filled by t0 + 7 min. A notice detected after t0 + 15 min has a missing entry; a short is never opened late.

U3 Marks and the exit are scheduled from the entry's fill time; each has a 10 min deadline. A missed one is recorded missing, and at most one later book walk of q (within 6 h) is kept as a separate late record.
U4 q is the size whose sale into the bids raises 100 USDC, rounded half-even to szDecimals; q = 0 is rejected. A book is stale when the receipt time minus the book's time exceeds 5 s.
U5 Funding boundaries are the hours in (entry, exit]. A fundingHistory record belongs to its nearest hour. oraclePx is read once per hour in [hour, hour + 60 s] for every position open at that hour.

U6 The Binance-prior exclusion counts an archive item published in [t0 - 24 h, t0] only through a version naming the token that was received at or before t0: the item itself (items.received_at) or a revision (item_revisions.received_at). It is checked at detection and again at t0 + 1 h. A version received after t0 (a late item, or a later revision naming the token) is listed as late, descriptive only, and never excludes.
U7 'In meta': a perp that nes_venues.hl_facts finds eligible but that today's meta lacks, or flags delisted, is ineligible (not_in_meta).

U8 The unclassified queue holds notices that mention 거래지원 or 마켓 with neither an addition nor an end (nes_classify.upbit_end) classification, and additions whose KRW membership the notice does not state.
U9 The monitor's first start is the epoch: archive cursors start at the archive's current maxima, and events with t0 before the epoch are not part of the measurement.

U10 The decision set is the first 40 comparable announcements in t0 order whose token-events are all final (an earlier event still open delays it), or on 2027-11-05 every comparable announcement with t0 before that date once all are final. It is recorded once in the ledger and never recomputed.

U11 Missed-detection audit: a KRW-* market new in market/all with no detected notice for that token whose t0 lies in [first seen - 7 d, first seen + 24 h]. market/all snapshots store the sorted market codes (stored once per distinct set) and every poll's time and hash.

U12 History reads are retried, then recorded unknown or missing: Binance klines and Hyperliquid leak candles up to t0 + 24 h, funding records up to exit + 24 h, hold candles up to exit + 48 h (Hyperliquid keeps about 3.5 days of 1 m candles).

U13 MAE/MFE use the 1 m candles that lie wholly inside the hold. The excursion is ok only with every expected minute; with fewer it is retried until exit + 48 h and then stored as partial (candles and expected counts, extrema under partial_* names), or missing with none.
U14 The tipping point is nes_returns.tipping_point at the same 95% level (a level argument with the old default was added for this).

U15 start_unknown is a stored event flag: no trading start was read (no body, or none parseable in it). It is never a comparable requirement and never makes an outcome missing. krw_market_first_seen_ms is the time of the first market_poll with obs_ms > t0 whose market set lists KRW-<TOKEN>, recorded once per event with the previous snapshot's time and whether that snapshot listed it (true only when the token was already on KRW).

U16 Evidence: a later Tree observation (duplicate item or revision) of an existing event's notice whose body states a start is appended as evidence:<event>:<ref> with a version number; the event id never changes. It counts for selection when no entry record exists yet and it was received by the entry deadline (t0 + 15 min). Among those and the event's own observation when it states a start, the latest by receipt (received_at, then items before item_revisions, then pk), not by processing order, sets the start. Otherwise its effect is descriptive.
U17 Binance presence and the leak test use only 1 m klines closed by t0 (open + 60 s <= t0); a candle that contains t0 is no evidence of a market before t0, and the next proxy candidate is tried.

preregistrations.spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-news-archive-design.md §6 @980236a, with §6.2 Hyperliquid eligibility amended by #237 (C1 option A, §11 call 14)
preregistrations.hypothesis: The demand shock overshoots and fades after the pump. Generated on data from before this window (below).

phase1: Window: announcements dated 2023-01-01 00:00 UTC to 2026-10-31 23:59 UTC. The start is roughly when Hyperliquid perps begin to exist. Nothing after the window enters this study.
Events, both Upbit studies (one shared manifest): one event per (notice, token) for Upbit `category=trade` notices whose title matches the KRW-market-addition pattern.
Tokens already on Upbit KRW are excluded.
So are tokens with a Binance catalog-48 listing announcement within ±24 h. That keeps the closed listing lane out of this sample.
Events whose Upbit KRW trading began before the notice are excluded too.
Timestamps:
Binance: `releaseDate`.
Upbit: the builder documents whether `listed_at` or `first_listed_at` is the publish time. The prereg names the field before Phase 1 runs.
Execution venues (Claude's call): Binance futures is CVM-blocked for the operator (see the `listing-reaction-study-2026-07` notes), so only these count:
Upbit fade (short): Hyperliquid perp only, under the same eligibility rule below. Spot-only tokens are excluded and counted, because Binance spot cannot short.

Hyperliquid eligibility needs positive pre-entry evidence (changed after both rounds; evidence source changed by §11 call 14). A token qualifies only if Hyperliquid hourly funding records (`fundingHistory`, by coin name) exist for it in the 24 h before t0, including at least one in the last hour before t0. Candles cannot serve: `candleSnapshot` returns only the most recent ~5,000 candles, which at 1 h reach back to about 2026-04 (probe on #229). Nothing after t0 is used for eligibility; using it would exclude exactly the tokens that become untradeable right after the event. Tokens no longer in today's `meta` are looked up by name through `fundingHistory`. The builder confirms in Phase 1 that this works for delisted coins and documents it.
Eligibility that cannot be verified is `unknown`. Unknown events are excluded and counted. An earliest daily candle alone is not enough.
Completeness evidence (changed after round 2).

Pagination (changed after round 3): each Binance catalog (48 and 161, plus monitoring if separate) and the Upbit list are harvested in full, every page. The harvested count must equal the API's reported `total`.
Any shortfall is added to the `missing` count, conservatively assumed to fall inside the window.
If no total is reported, the study is INCONCLUSIVE-by-data.
This also covers the catalog-48 overlap exclusion.

Observed 2026-11-03: Upbit's Cloudflare answered error 1015 to page requests 1.5 s apart, so the full Upbit harvest runs at least 8 s per page. Binance catalog 161 reported `total` 446, and its oldest article is dated 2022-02-17.

Candles (changed after round 3): the exact 1m candles each calculation uses must exist. These are t0−10 min and t0−2 min for the leak test, the entry candle, and each horizon's exit candle. No interpolation and no forward-fill. If any is missing, and the halt rule does not resolve it, the event is `missing`.
Halts after entry (changed after rounds 3–4): if an exit candle is missing because trading halted, the exit is the first candle after trading resumes, within 72 h of that scheduled exit time.
Costs are always subtracted from the net return, whatever the side, never applied to a price.
If trading does not resume within that window, the event is `unresolved`.
`halted` events stay in every criterion.

Any unresolved event makes the study INCONCLUSIVE (changed after rounds 4–5). Their outcomes are outcome-dependent: terminal delistings would vanish. So with one or more `unresolved` events the result is INCONCLUSIVE. There is no imputation shortcut: imputed values can move the median and concentration criteria in either direction.
Coverage gate: `unknown`, `missing` and `unresolved` together above 20% of candidate events make the study INCONCLUSIVE-by-data. So does harvesting that cannot complete within the shared limiter.
Resource budget for Part C (changed after round 3):
Harvesting, downloading, decompressing and analysis run under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1G -p CPUQuota=50%` with `nice` and `ionice -c3`.
Before each download batch, the 15 GB free-disk guard from §4.4 applies.

Only the daily kline files covering each event's [t0−1 d, t0+5 d] window are downloaded. That covers entry+24 h plus the 72 h resumption window. Each zip is deleted after the needed rows are extracted.
The expected footprint is under 1 GB.

Symbols and price series: the manifest freezes the token → Binance-symbol mapping, including 1000-prefixed contracts and renames, and which proxy series each event will use. Proxy series are Binance 1m klines from `data.binance.vision`, USDⓈ-M futures preferred, spot otherwise. Phase 1 checks only that the series exists; it computes no returns.
Events with missing proxy data are excluded and counted toward the coverage gate above.
Freeze: the manifest file's SHA-256 is recorded in a preregistration amendment, merged before Phase 2 starts.
phase2: Entry latency (changed after review): taker entry at the close of the 1m candle containing t+5 min. Five minutes covers detection by a 60 s poller on Tree plus processing. A t+60 s entry is reported as descriptive only, because the archive's own Binance rotation could not detect that fast.
Exits: the fixed horizons entry+30 min, entry+4 h and entry+24 h.

Costs: taker fees of 4.5 bps per side on Hyperliquid or 7.5 bps on Binance spot, plus 10 bps per side of slippage. A stress case at 25 bps per side is reported. Hyperliquid funding is not modelled; at the +4 h primary horizon it is about four hourly payments. This is listed as a limitation.

Proxy status: the returns come from Binance prices, not Hyperliquid fills. Basis and impact are not measured, so any result is labelled a proxy result. That is acceptable only because a pass authorizes nothing beyond a paper forward monitor, and that monitor measures executable prices.

The forward monitor keeps each event's venue assignment (changed after round 2). It uses Hyperliquid best bid/offer (BBO) for Hyperliquid-assigned events and Binance spot `bookTicker` for spot-assigned Upbit events. So a pass driven by spot events is validated on spot, not on a different subset.
Leak flag: reuse the listing study's rule: more than 2% absolute drift over [t0−10 min, t0−2 min]. The primary set excludes leaked events; a sensitivity run includes them.
Unit of analysis (changed after review): the announcement, not the token. One Binance notice often names several tokens.
Each announcement's return is the mean net return of its eligible tokens.
The chronological halves split announcements by date.
Primary horizon: +4 h, declared now.
Pass (all required, evaluated at +4 h after fees and 10 bps slippage):
at least 20 distinct announcements in the primary set;
announcement-level median net return > 0;
a positive median in both chronological halves;
the top decile of announcements contributes less than 60% of the sum of announcement returns. This criterion fails whenever that sum is ≤ 0.
Also reported, not criteria:
a bootstrap 95% CI of the announcement-level median (10,000 resamples);
BTC-adjusted returns;

for the two short studies, the per-event maximum adverse excursion from entry to each exit, from 1m highs. A short's risk sits in the squeeze tail, which the median does not show. This is descriptive only: a missing candle inside the path makes that event's MAE unavailable. It never changes return eligibility, the coverage gate, aggregation or pass/fail;
all three horizons, both halves, per venue and per notice kind;
leak and slippage sensitivities;
excluded, unknown and missing counts.
Separate hypotheses. The studies are never pooled, and a pass in one is not evidence for another.
The Upbit long and fade share their Hyperliquid events. On that subset the fade's net return is the long's gross return with the sign flipped, minus costs.
So a failed long plus a passed fade is one finding, not two confirmations.

Kill: with at least 20 announcements, any failed criterion closes that lane for this config. A pass authorizes only a paper forward monitor, preregistered separately, in the `listing-short-forward` style.

Too few announcements (Claude's call): fewer than 20 is INCONCLUSIVE-by-data, the precedent from the listing study's Hyperliquid venue. The lane stays open, but nothing is authorized: no monitor and no bot. The archive keeps recording these events. Any re-test is a new, forward-only preregistration; retrospective and forward events are never mixed.
Code and data:
Code lives in the repo under `research/news_event_studies/`.
Downloaded klines and results stay on the VPS under `research/news_event_studies/data/`, gitignored.
The resolution is written into the prereg entry mechanically, from the frozen criteria only.
fade_origin: Why the fade was added (2026-11-03, before any Phase 1 work). An exploratory check on 2018–2022 data, all of it before this window, covered 42 token events in 33 Upbit KRW-addition notices, all for tokens already on Binance spot ([#229 comment](https://github.com/IvPalmer/Master-Trader/issues/229#issuecomment-6617239337)).
The median Binance price was already +11% by t+5 min.
A long from t+5 min lost. These are token-level medians net of costs, BTC-hedged: −4.5% at +4 h and −6.3% at +24 h, with 19% of events positive at +24 h. Unhedged, they were −3.7% and −7.4%.
This study does not use those statistics. Its decision metric stays the registered one: unadjusted, announcement-level net returns.
The operator asked for the inverse to be preregistered.
The 2018–2022 sample is the hypothesis source. It never counts as validation and is never mixed with this window.

The long study stays registered exactly as written. The fade reuses its Phase 1 manifest and every Phase 2 rule: entry, horizons, primary horizon, costs, leak flag, unit of analysis and pass criteria. Only two things differ: the direction, and the venue rule (Hyperliquid only).

operationalization: O1 t0: Binance `releaseDate` (ms); Upbit `first_listed_at` (KST→UTC). `listed_at` moves when a notice is edited (Part A: id 6687, 21:50 vs 20:00 KST).

O2 price_at(X) = the close of the Binance 1m candle whose open is floor_minute(X). Entry = price_at(t0+300 s); exit_H = price_at(t0+300 s+H). Leak drift = price_at(t0−120 s) / price_at(t0−600 s) − 1, in exact decimals; leaked if |drift| > 0.02.
O3 Gross long = exit/entry − 1; gross short = −(exit/entry − 1); net = gross − 2 × (fee + slippage) / 10,000.

O4 Missing candles: a missing exit candle → the close of the first candle opening in (scheduled, scheduled + 72 h] = `halted`; none → `unresolved`. Exception: when that candle exists but the scheduled exit's UTC-day file is absent (HTTP 404), the gap is an archive hole and the event is `missing`. A missing leak or entry candle → `missing`. Event status, strongest first: `unresolved` at any horizon, then `missing`, then `halted` at any horizon, else `ok`.

O5 Hyperliquid eligibility: `fundingHistory` by coin name, with candidates [T, "k"+T] and names containing ":" skipped. Queries cover [t0−24 h, t0−1 ms]. eligible: ≥ 1 evidence time in [t0−24 h, t0) and ≥ 1 in [t0−1 h, t0). Evidence times are candle close `T` for candles and `time` for funding records; ineligible: no such evidence. A name absent from today's `meta` that also returns none is ineligible (`never_in_meta`); for such a name, HTTP 500 with body `null` counts as returning none (probe (f) on #229), and any other failed response stops the build; unknown: the evidence cannot be fetched or lies beyond retention (candle mode: t0−24 h earlier than BTC's earliest 1h candle); an unknown status excludes the event from all three studies.

O6 Binance presence: a daily 1m file on `data.binance.vision` for the UTC day before date(t0), for some candidate symbol. Candidates: UM futures `T`, `1000T`, `1000000T`, `1MT` + `USDT`; spot `T`, `1000T`, `1MT` + `USDT`. The Binance-spot venue needs a spot file for that day.

O7 Proxy: the first candidate, all UM futures before spot, with files for every UTC date from date(t0−1 d) to date(t0+2 d). Failing that, the first candidate in the same order with files for date(t0−1 d) and date(t0); its later gaps go through O4, so a series that ends after entry is `unresolved`, never `missing`. None → `missing`.
O8 Upbit KRW addition: a title with a KRW marker (`KRW` or `원화`) and an addition marker (`디지털 자산 추가`, `신규 상장` or `신규 거래지원`), containing none of 종료/유의/제거/변경/중단/연기/재개.
O9 Already on Upbit KRW: an earlier harvested KRW-addition notice for the token, with no KRW trading-end notice (`거래지원 종료`, `상장폐지` or `상장 폐지`, not limited to BTC/USDT markets) between it and t0.

O10 Upbit trading began before the notice: the trading-start time stated in the notice body is earlier than t0. A body with no parseable start time makes the event `unknown`. The start is read from the token's row of a table whose header has `거래지원 개시 시점` (or `거래 지원 개시 시점`), else from a line containing `거래지원 개시`, `거래 지원 개시` or `거래 오픈`; clocks are `HH:MM` or `H시 M분`, in KST. A start stated without a year takes the year (t0's KST year, or the one before or after) that puts it nearest t0; a tie is `unknown` (probe on #229: `10월 27일 16시 40분 예정` in a table cell).
O11 Catalog-48 overlap: any catalog-48 title naming the token within ±24 h of t0, inclusive.
O12 Delisting events come from harvested titles only. Overlap is computed over the full harvest before the window filter. A notice ≤ 24 h after the token's last kept notice is dropped.

O13 Coverage = (unknown + missing + unresolved + harvest shortfall) / (token-events not excluded by a verified rule + harvest shortfall). Above 0.20 → INCONCLUSIVE-by-data. A catalog-48 shortfall counts for both Upbit studies.
O14 Statistics: halves: announcements sorted by (t0, id), the first floor(n/2) against the rest; top decile: the ceil(n/10) largest announcement returns; median: `statistics.median`.
O15 Reported only: the bootstrap uses 10,000 resamples with `random.Random(229)`, 2.5/97.5 percentiles of the median. BTC adjustment uses BTCUSDT UM futures with β = 1.

O16 Harvest completeness: a full Binance catalog = pages 1..ceil(total/50), plus a closing page-1 fetch; complete when unique ids ≥ the closing `total`; two limiter suspensions, or 72 h without completing, mean the harvest cannot complete → INCONCLUSIVE-by-data; Upbit is harvested from the operator's Mac, and the manifest records the host.
O17 Monitoring-tag notices come from catalog 161. Catalog 49 is scanned back to 2023-01-01, and a monitoring-tag title found there stops Phase 1 for an operator decision.
pass_criteria: at least 20 distinct announcements in the primary set;
a positive median in both chronological halves;
the top decile of announcements contributes less than 60% of the sum of announcement returns. This criterion fails whenever that sum is ≤ 0.
preregistrations.kill: Kill: with at least 20 announcements, any failed criterion closes that lane for this config. A pass authorizes only a paper forward monitor, preregistered separately, in the `listing-short-forward` style.
inconclusive: Too few announcements (Claude's call): fewer than 20 is INCONCLUSIVE-by-data, the precedent from the listing study's Hyperliquid venue. The lane stays open, but nothing is authorized: no monitor and no bot. The archive keeps recording these events. Any re-test is a new, forward-only preregistration; retrospective and forward events are never mixed.

INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL, when the data cannot decide. This applies in three cases: fewer than 20 announcements; `unknown`, `missing` and `unresolved` events together above 20% of candidates; or any `unresolved` post-entry event at all. Nothing is authorized, and any re-test is forward-only (§6.2).
rules: Research only: no deploy, config, sizing or allocation change follows from any result; a PASS authorizes only a separately preregistered paper forward monitor.

rulings: upbit 3502 'KRW, BTC 마켓 디지털 자산 추가 (SUI) (매도 주문 제한 기준 가격 안내)': a parenthetical ending in 안내 or 마켓 is a note, not a token, so SUI is the token.
upbit 4273 '테더(USDT) KRW, BTC 마켓 추가 안내 (출금 개시 안내)' has none of the O8 addition markers, so it is not a KRW addition.

O8 per token: when one notice adds several tokens to several markets, a token is a KRW addition only when the notice puts that token on KRW. The evidence is, in order: the title's market group for that token; a title naming only the KRW market, or a single-token title; the notice body (a 마켓 table column, '- TOKEN : KRW 마켓' or '- KRW 마켓 : TOKEN, …'). A token added to BTC or USDT only is neither an event nor an O9 prior. A token whose market is unstated is not a prior before the window and needs review inside it. amendments.decision_rule: Classification on the announcement-level mean net return at +4 h, primary set (leak test run and passed). EDGE (proxy): the Bonferroni-adjusted (3 studies, 98.33% two-sided) percentile interval of the stress-cost (25 bps per side) mean, from 10,000 calendar-month block-bootstrap resamples (seed 229), lies above zero. NO EDGE: the same interval of the base-cost (10 bps) mean lies at or below zero. Otherwise NOT DETERMINABLE, which includes fewer than two calendar months. The decision metric is the raw (unhedged) net mean; the median and the BTC-adjusted mean (beta 1, no hedge cost) are descriptive.
amendments.missing_outcomes: The class assumes missing outcomes resemble observed ones. Missing = token-events in the primary population (leak test not run, or passed with no usable +4 h return) plus Phase 1 unknown/missing token-events, counted per token, including announcements that are only partly missing. The report gives the tipping point: the common return of every missing token-event, with each announcement keeping its token weights, at which the class would stop holding.

reasons: Placebo coverage: shifting triggers by up to 30 days pulled them across the ends of the data (ES history starts 2024-06-14, the fetch ends 2026-11-05), so shifted guards saw fewer triggers near the window edges and could inflate the real guard's rank.

changes.trigger_scope: triggers are used only inside the variant's window (window_intraday_utc or window_daily_utc), for the real guard and the placebos alike
changes.placebo: each of the 60 whole-day shifts in +/-1..placebo_max_days applied to every in-window trigger, wrapping circularly within the window (whole-day shifts of a whole-day window keep the hour of day); enumerated, no random draw. Exact one-sided rank p: p_helps = (1 + #placebo changes >= real) / 61, p_hurts = (1 + #placebo changes <= real) / 61; the percentile (ties half) is reported for continuity
